copy: If constipation started after your GLP-1, buying another remedy may not answer the question you actually have: why does your digestion feel so different now?
visual: P01: Consistent female AI presenter, early 50s, seated at an ordinary kitchen table, close eye-level phone framing. Empty hands; no bottles or gummies. Small AI-presenter disclosure.
cut: Open directly on the first word. Hold eye contact through the question.
purpose: Recognize the viewer's experience and open a specific explanation loop.

copy: The scale is moving. But you're counting days between bathroom trips, feeling uncomfortable after meals, and wondering what to try next. You wanted to spend less time thinking about your weight. Now you're thinking about your stomach.
visual: B01: Overhead hand marks an ordinary calendar, without a promised result date. B02: Side-angle dining scene, woman sets down her fork and shifts in her chair. P01 returns for the final sentence.
cut: Cut on 'counting days'; change to B02 on 'after meals'; return to presenter on 'You wanted'.
purpose: Connect the physical complaint to the lost freedom the viewer wants back.
proof: Illustrative situations, not a customer testimonial or before/after.

copy: GLP-1 medicines can slow stomach emptying. Constipation is also a known side effect. And when you're eating less, your usual fiber and fluid intake can change, too. That gives you more to consider than simply choosing a stronger laxative.
visual: B03: One clean side-section stomach illustration showing slower emptying, labeled 'Illustration'. B04: Overhead comparison of an ordinary meal and a smaller portion, with a water glass. Never depict a stopped or paralyzed bowel.
cut: Move to B03 on 'slow stomach emptying'; move to B04 on 'eating less'. Return to P01 for the last sentence.
purpose: Give a comprehensible explanation without turning one physiological effect into the cause of every symptom.
proof: Wegovy prescribing information; NIDDK dietary context. Does not prove any Motilli effect.

copy: Fiber, stool softeners, and stimulant laxatives have different jobs. They aren't interchangeable. If what you've tried hasn't helped, your prescriber can help you work out the next step.
visual: B05: Three plain category cards on a tabletop, each separated by a hand. No branded OTC packs, red X, or imagery of fiber becoming a blockage. P01 delivers prescriber sentence.
cut: Cut to the category cards on the three-item list; return on 'If what'.
purpose: Preserve the reference's explanation of disappointing attempts without claiming legitimate treatments universally fail.

copy: For everyday digestive supplements, there are three things worth checking: the ingredients, what they're there for, and how easily the routine fits your day. Take prebiotic fiber. It feeds certain beneficial bacteria already living in your gut. That's a different role from a stimulant laxative.
visual: P01 counts three checks on fingers. B06: Distinct close microscopic illustration of microbes using prebiotic substrate; no stomach, no product, no before/after transformation. Caption 'Prebiotic fiber: food for certain gut bacteria'.
cut: Keep checklist on presenter; cut to B06 on 'Take prebiotic fiber'; return for the final sentence.
purpose: Teach a category role and establish purchase criteria before introducing a brand.
proof: ISAPP prebiotic definition; category evidence only. No dose-specific or finished-product efficacy claim.

copy: You already have enough to organize around your shot. A daily supplement should be easy to understand and easy to take.
visual: P01, consistent kitchen and wardrobe, slightly wider framing. Hands remain empty. No product silhouette, logo, gummy or product-page insert.
cut: Stay with presenter; leave a short natural pause before the brand reveal.
purpose: Connect the criteria to a practical product reason without teasing an unsupported cure.

copy: That's the idea behind Motilli Celery Juice Gummies. The formula combines celery juice powder, chlorophyll, and FOS, a prebiotic fiber. And the daily serving is just two gummies.
visual: P02: FIRST product visibility and spoken name together. Same presenter brings the accurately referenced bottle into frame on 'Motilli'. B07: Distinct tabletop composition with actual bottle and typeset ingredient list. B08: Macro of two correctly shaped gummies in an open palm.
cut: First bottle pixel on spoken 'Motilli', never before. Ingredient list on 'formula combines'; gummy macro on 'two gummies'.
purpose: Reveal the product as an example of the criteria already taught; make the format concrete.
proof: Current Motilli product page for listed ingredients, format and directions. Supplier/label references required before generated product visuals.

copy: No drink to mix. No capsule to swallow. The directions are simple: two gummies before bed with a full glass of water. You can read the ingredients and serving directions before you decide.
visual: B09: Unique bedside three-quarter view; hand places two gummies beside a full glass of water. B10: Accurate label close-up with serving directions, typeset separately if needed for legibility. No simulated customer results.
cut: Cut to bedtime setup on 'directions'; label close-up on 'read the ingredients'.
purpose: Resolve effort and transparency objections with demonstrable product facts.
proof: PDP directions. This is product demonstration, not clinical or outcome proof.

visual: P02 holds bottle naturally. Typeset '90-day money-back guarantee from delivery' and 'Includes opened bottles. See refund policy for terms.' No seal implying clinical certification.
cut: Return to presenter on 'Motilli also'; hold readable guarantee text throughout.
purpose: Reduce purchase risk using the actual policy.
proof: Refund policy effective August 2026; request approval and any requested return still apply.
